summary: Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Japan Women's University (~1944–1948) and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1981–1987).
Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies. His career includes attested appointments in 2015 as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Takahiko Sato (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Koyasan University, where his post is attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Kato (born 1974) is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Holding a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, he serves as a professor at the University of Tokyo and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Takako Abe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Taisho University as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University and studied abroad in 1978 at UH Mānoa and IBS. He was professor of Shin Buddhist studies and president (1989–1995) at Ryukoku, and chaired BDK.

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Waseda University, earning a doctorate in literature (-1931), and at the University of Paris (~1916–1920). He served as an English teacher, lecturer, and dean of the Faculty of Letters (1930) at Waseda.

Takami Inoue works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami and pursued doctoral studies at Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama. He later served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University.

Takanobu Takahashi (born 1951) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University (PhD 1985–1988). He held associate professorships at Shitennoji University and the University of Tokyo (1999–2016).

Takanori Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and holds an appointment as a special appointment lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani (born 1948) is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and later held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2011–2018).

Takanori Unno (born 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies and a doctorate at Nagoya University, studying under Yoshifumi Ueda and Hidenori Kitagawa, among others. He held academic posts at Nagoya, Aichi Prefectural, and Meijo Universities.

Takao Hayashi (born 1949) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku and Kyoto Universities before earning his PhD at Brown under David Pingree in 1985. He was an assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015) at Doshisha University.
Takao Kagawa (born 1926) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama (born 1929) specializes in Buddhist studies and completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held professorships at Rissho University (~1975–1983), Shinshu University (~1983–1988; later professor emeritus), and Mejiro University (~1988–2000).

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Osaka University, where he served as an associate professor (1984) and professor (1994–2012).

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1951–1959). He served on the faculty at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1971–2000) and was president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata (born 1944), an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (Dr. Phil.) under Lambert Schmithausen and Albrecht Wezler. He served as associate professor (~1987–1992) and professor (~1992–2015) at Waseda University.
Takashi Koezuka (born 1939) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 2001) and was later named professor emeritus (attested 2012).
